core.summary: Sequence manipulation shared by most workflows

seqkit.summary: FASTA/FASTQ toolkit: sequence statistics, filtering, sampling, format conversion, and subsequence extraction. Strand-aware operations keep the recorded strand; do not assume forward orientation.

seqtk.summary: Minimal FASTA/FASTQ converter and sampler: format conversion, subsampling, reverse complement, and region extraction. Prints usage instead of a version banner, so no version argument is used.

samtools.summary: SAM/BAM/CRAM manipulation: view, sort, index, flagstat, depth, faidx. Region-based access requires an index (.bai/.csi); report read strand explicitly when converting to sequence.

fastp.summary: FASTQ quality control and adapter trimming with HTML/JSON reports. Runtime grows with file size; submit through the job channel rather than a synchronous call.

bcftools.summary: VCF/BCF manipulation: view, query, filter, merge, norm, annotate, stats. Allele-specific fields use Number=A/R/G conventions, so multiallelic records must not be assumed biallelic.

bedtools.summary: Genomic interval arithmetic: intersect, merge, subtract, closest, coverage, getfasta. BED coordinates are 0-based half-open while GFF/VCF are 1-based, so conversions must be explicit. Stranded operations require -s and report the strand column.

minimap2.summary: Long-read and spliced nucleotide alignment. Hours-scale on whole genomes, so it belongs in a generated workflow executed by the user, not in an interactive session. Presets (map-ont, map-hifi, sr, splice) must match the sequencing technology.

bwa.summary: Burrows-Wheeler short-read aligner (mem/mem2). Whole-genome alignment takes hours, so generate a workflow rather than running it interactively. Requires a prebuilt index; prints usage instead of a version banner.

bowtie2.summary: Short-read aligner with sensitive/very-sensitive presets, strong for paired-end data and local alignment. Whole-genome runs are hours-scale and belong in a generated workflow.

mafft.summary: Multiple sequence alignment with automatic strategy selection (auto mode) plus L-INS-i/G-INS-i for accuracy. Runtime grows quickly with sequence count, so medium sets go through the job channel.

notes: License identifiers must be verified against each upstream repository LICENSE before wiring a new tool in; the loader rejects AGPL and non-commercial entries.
Platforms use micromamba identifiers. bioconda has no win-64 builds for these tools, so Windows reaches them through WSL or a remote host.
run_mode drives routing: sync runs in-process, job submits and polls, external only produces a workflow definition for the user to execute.
An existing system installation is always preferred over the private prefix; set min_version on an entry to force a fallback only when the system build is too old.
conda_name and executable paths follow bioconda conventions and must be confirmed on the target machine; a wrong package name surfaces as a solver error in bioenv/logs rather than a silent failure.
help_args set to an empty array means the tool has no usable help flag (bwa, seqtk); such tools skip the mandatory help observation instead of being blocked forever.
